# Configure Vault credential injection

Integrating Boundary and Vault allows you to inject credentials directly into sessions. Credential injection provides a passwordless experience for end users, as Boundary handles the retrieval and injection of credentials behind the scenes. This prevents credentials from being exposed to the client machine.

This page shows you how to integrate Boundary with Vault's KV, SSH certificate, and LDAP secrets engines for credential injection.

## Requirements

Before configuring credential injection with Vault, ensure you have:

- A running Vault instance with an address reachable from your Boundary controllers or workers.
- A configured Vault credential store in Boundary. Refer to [Create a Vault credential store](/boundary/docs/credentials/static-cred-vault).
- An existing target in Boundary configured for SSH, RDP, or other sessions. Refer to [Configure targets with credential injection](/boundary/docs/credentials/configure-credential-injection).

## Vault KV secrets engine

The Vault Key-Value (KV) secrets engine stores static credentials, such as username/password pairs or SSH private keys. When a session starts, Boundary retrieves the static secret from Vault and injects it directly.

### 1. Configure Vault

Enable the KV secrets engine (version 2 is recommended) and write a secret:

```shell-session
$ vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2

$ vault kv put secret/boundary/ssh-credentials \
    username="ubuntu" \
    private_key="-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
```

### 2. Configure Boundary

Create a generic Vault credential library in Boundary pointing to the secret path.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

Create the credential library using the `vault-generic` type:

```shell-session
$ boundary credential-libraries create vault-generic \
    -name "vault-kv-ssh" \
    -description "KV secrets engine for SSH injection" \
    -credential-store-id csvlt_1234567890 \
    -credential-type ssh_private_key \
    -vault-path "secret/data/boundary/ssh-credentials" \
    -vault-http-method "GET"
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Use the `boundary_credential_library_vault` resource to define the generic credential library:

```hcl
resource "boundary_credential_library_vault" "kv_ssh" {
  name                = "vault-kv-ssh"
  description         = "KV secrets engine for SSH injection"
  credential_store_id = boundary_credential_store_vault.example.id
  path                = "secret/data/boundary/ssh-credentials"
  http_method         = "GET"
  credential_type     = "ssh_private_key"
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Vault SSH certificate secrets engine

The Vault SSH secrets engine can act as a Certificate Authority (CA) to sign SSH keys dynamically. This allows Boundary to generate short-lived, self-defending SSH certificates for every target connection, ensuring access is secure and auditable without managing static credentials.

There are two primary modes depending on the endpoint used:
- `/issue`: Vault generates the private/public key pair and returns the signed certificate and private key.
- `/sign`: Boundary controllers generate the key pair and send only the public key to Vault to sign.

### 1. Configure Vault

Mount the SSH secrets engine, configure its CA, and define a signing role:

```shell-session
# 1. Enable the SSH secrets engine
$ vault secrets enable -path=ssh-client-signer ssh

# 2. Configure Vault as the SSH Certificate Authority (CA)
$ vault write ssh-client-signer/config/ca generate_signing_key=true

# 3. Create a role for signing client keys
$ vault write ssh-client-signer/roles/boundary-client \
    key_type=ca \
    algorithm_signer=rsa-sha2-512 \
    allow_user_certificates=true \
    allowed_users="*" \
    default_extensions="permit-pty" \
    ttl=30m
```

### 2. Configure Boundary

Create an SSH certificate credential library in Boundary pointing to the signing role path.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

Create the SSH certificate credential library using the `vault-ssh-certificate` type. Point `-vault-path` to the `/sign/role-name` endpoint:

```shell-session
$ boundary credential-libraries create vault-ssh-certificate \
    -name "vault-ssh-certs" \
    -description "Dynamic SSH certificate injection" \
    -credential-store-id csvlt_1234567890 \
    -vault-path "ssh-client-signer/sign/boundary-client" \
    -username "ubuntu" \
    -key-type "ed25519" \
    -additional-valid-principal "ec2-user" \
    -extension "permit-pty="
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Use the `boundary_credential_library_vault_ssh_certificate` resource to define the library:

```hcl
resource "boundary_credential_library_vault_ssh_certificate" "ssh_certs" {
  name                = "vault-ssh-certs"
  description         = "Dynamic SSH certificate injection"
  credential_store_id = boundary_credential_store_vault.example.id
  path                = "ssh-client-signer/sign/boundary-client"
  username            = "ubuntu"
  key_type            = "ed25519"
  
  extensions = {
    permit-pty = ""
  }

  additional_valid_principals = [
    "ec2-user"
  ]
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Vault LDAP secrets engine

The Vault LDAP secrets engine can generate temporary LDAP credentials. When a session starts, Boundary requests dynamic or static credentials from Vault's LDAP secrets engine, allowing users to authenticate seamlessly against Active Directory or OpenLDAP.

### 1. Configure Vault

Mount the LDAP secrets engine, configure its connection parameters, and define an LDAP role:

```shell-session
# 1. Enable the LDAP secrets engine
$ vault secrets enable ldap

# 2. Configure connection settings for the LDAP server
$ vault write ldap/config \
    binddn="cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org" \
    bindpass="admin-password" \
    url="ldap://ldap.example.org:389" \
    userdn="ou=people,dc=example,dc=org" \
    schema="openldap"

# 3. Create an LDAP role
$ vault write ldap/role/boundary-role \
    username="boundary-user"
```

### 2. Configure Boundary

Create an LDAP credential library in Boundary pointing to the LDAP role path.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

Create the LDAP credential library using the `vault-ldap` type:

```shell-session
$ boundary credential-libraries create vault-ldap \
    -name "vault-ldap-creds" \
    -description "LDAP secrets engine integration" \
    -credential-store-id csvlt_1234567890 \
    -vault-path "ldap/static-cred/boundary-role"
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Use the `boundary_credential_library_vault_ldap` resource to define the library:

```hcl
resource "boundary_credential_library_vault_ldap" "ldap_creds" {
  name                = "vault-ldap-creds"
  description         = "LDAP secrets engine integration"
  credential_store_id = boundary_credential_store_vault.example.id
  path                = "ldap/static-cred/boundary-role"
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
